candidates.pronunciation: MEH-zhurd moht; initial /m/ repeated across the two words
candidates.grammar: Two-word noun phrase; master or library name, with the category descriptor supplied separately rather than implied by the sound figure.
candidates.rationale: The repeated /m/ onset is deliberate alliteration: it makes a small, countable unit memorable while 'Measured' keeps evaluation visible. The mote image is modest enough not to imply proof, autonomy, or a universal platform.
candidates.etymology: English words measured and mote; no borrowed technical or cultural source.
known_concerns: The /zh/ sound in measured is hard to recover from speech for some international users.
Mote can make a serious evaluation library sound tiny or toy-like.
The space is not itself a Hex or OTP identifier.
notes: challenge_cell:3-sound-figures; mechanism_subtype: precise alliteration on /m/; stance: affirmative; scope: current.

spoken_dictation: say 'MEH-zhurd moht'; a listener may write Measured Mode or Measure Mote; dictation should pause between words. accessibility: screen readers have ordinary word pronunciations, but the /zh/ phoneme and pairwise alliteration do not convey meaning by sound alone.
code_forms: hex_package=measured_mote; otp_app=:measured_mote; module_root=MeasuredMote; mix_task_prefix=measured_mote; config_prefix=:measured_mote; telemetry_prefix=[:measured_mote, ...].

product_truth: the name can truthfully sit on the pre-release Elixir library and OTP application documented here. current_embodiment: signatures, programs, calls, evaluation, and optimizer flows remain the actual boundary. horizon_embodiment: a future artifact-optimization substrate may reuse the identity for instructions or demonstrations only conditionally, with no claim of autonomous improvement.
